items.title: 5.4.1 Instantaneous dipole-induced dipole forces (London dispersion forces)

source_refs.note: Topic 5.4.1, printed pages 98-100 (Tables 5.1 and 5.2, Figure 5.2), with Quick Check 5.2 as the self-check. The print's 'Isodecane (C20H42)' is icosane.

blocks.title: Instantaneous dipole-induced dipole force
blocks.text: The momentary force of attraction between an instantaneous dipole and an induced dipole is called the instantaneous dipole-induced dipole force (id-id). These are the only forces that exist among the molecules of non-polar compounds.

When the molecular mass of a compound is greater, the id-id forces are stronger, and vice versa, because in a larger atom or molecule the dispersion of the electron cloud and its polarization is easier. This factor operates in the halogen and noble gas families: the physical state changes down the halogen family as size and polarizability increase, fluorine and chlorine being gases, bromine a liquid and iodine a solid (boiling point 458 K), and the boiling points of the noble gases rise from helium to xenon.

blocks.caption: Molar masses and boiling points of groups 17 and 18 (Table 5.1)

blocks.text: A molecule with a larger surface area has more points of contact with a nearby molecule, so the forces among molecules of larger surface area are stronger. In the saturated hydrocarbons, chains of carbon atoms linked to hydrogen, ethane C2H6 boils at -88.6 degrees C and hexane C6H14 at 68.7 degrees C: longer molecules have more places along their length where they can be attracted to other molecules. The three isomers of pentane have the same relative molecular mass but differ in surface area: straight-chain n-pentane has the largest surface area and the highest boiling point (36.2 degrees C), 2-methylbutane (isopentane) a smaller area (28 degrees C), and 2,2-dimethylpropane (neopentane) the smallest and the weakest forces (9.5 degrees C).

blocks.alt: Carbon skeletons of the three isomers of C5H12 with a shaded outline of each molecule's surface. n-Pentane is a long zigzag chain (boiling point 36.2 C), 2-methylbutane has one branch (28 C), and 2,2-dimethylpropane is almost ball-shaped (9.5 C). The more surface contact, the stronger the London forces and the higher the boiling point.
